verdict.rationale: PayPal's ACP/Braintree flow does issue a scoped, single-use delegated token — 'bound to your merchant ID and includes amount and time restrictions that you can configure' — which matches the spirit of a scoped credential rather than a raw card number, and UCP similarly hands off a tokenized, single-use credential. However, this is merchant-side infrastructure (issued per-checkout by the merchant/Braintree flow), not a user-controlled credential the AI-native end user personally hands to their own agent with self-set limits; there's no consumer-facing UI or API for an end user to mint/configure their own scoped card-like token independent of a specific merchant checkout. missing for 10: end-user-facing tooling to create/configure a personal scoped credential (not merchant-issued per-transaction token), explicit merchant-restriction controls set by the user, and independent/hands-on confirmation of the token's real-world limits.
